title: In this world, every lie you've ever told floats above your head.
formula: Strange act (3 weeks of silence) -> rule + goal (the girl at zero) -> rival with a 'perfect' number who mocks you (planted: he never takes off his hat) -> your plan, rule taken literally against you (a nod counts) -> it works, rival loses the date -> big test with the rival watching -> the truth raises your number (it counts what's true) -> rival's laugh knocks her beehive off: her real number -> loop: you finally speak, and there's no ding
loop: Line 1: you haven't said a single word in 3 weeks. Last: for the first time in 3 weeks you speak, and the counter stays silent (no ding): the silence flips from you to the rule.
facts: Fiction: no sources needed. Rule: a glowing number floats just above each person's head and counts every lie they have ever told, in words or not. It goes up the moment they lie and never goes down.

lines.narration: You haven't said a single word in 3 *weeks*.
lines.spoken: You haven't said a single word in three weeks.
lines.scene: Cold open, busy office: everyone chatting; you at your desk, lips pressed shut, a cartoon zipper across your mouth. Above your head, a huge glowing '4,000'.
lines.camera: Slow push-in between two chatting coworkers to you
lines.gag: A literal zipper across your mouth

lines.narration: Because in this world, every lie you've ever told floats over your head, and yours says *4,000*.
lines.spoken: Because in this world, every lie you've ever told floats over your head, and yours says four thousand.
lines.scene: Street outside: every passer-by has a small glowing number; yours is the biggest thing on the block. A pigeon stares at it.
lines.camera: Crane up from you to the street full of numbers
lines.gag: The pigeon slowly side-eyes your number

lines.narration: The girl from the coffee shop is at a perfect *zero*.
lines.scene: Golden morning coffee shop: a barista with a yellow beanie and paint on her sleeves, a soft '0' above her like a halo.
lines.camera: Dolly in, shallow focus
lines.gag: Her 0 glows like a halo; a choir card pops

lines.narration: And Pam from HR is at 12. She never takes her hair down, and she never lets you *forget* it.
lines.scene: Pam leans on your desk: cardigan, reading glasses on a chain, a towering beehive; a neat '12' glows right at the top of the beehive. She taps your 4,000 with a pen.
lines.camera: Low angle on Pam, tilt up her tall beehive
lines.gag: Pam's beehive is absurdly tall, like a chimney
lines.spoken: And Pam from HR is at twelve. She never takes her hair down, and she never lets you forget it.

lines.narration: "Nice number, liar," she says, and sets the coffee girl up on a date with her *nephew*.
lines.scene: Coffee shop: Pam leans over the counter, beehive brushing the ceiling lamp, showing her a photo of her nephew; you stand behind Pam in the queue.
lines.camera: Over your shoulder, push past you to Pam
lines.gag: Pam's beehive knocks the lamp swinging

lines.narration: So you've made a plan: no talking, no lies, no new *numbers*.
lines.scene: Your bedroom wall, night: a crayon plan with three boxes, 'NO TALKING', 'NO LIES', and a crossed-out speech bubble.
lines.camera: Pan across the wall plan
lines.gag: Your plan is drawn in crayon

lines.narration: It's going great, until your boss asks if you like his new *haircut*.
lines.scene: Office: your boss leans over your desk, proud of an awful bowl cut with one long strand.
lines.camera: Low angle on the boss
lines.gag: The haircut has one strand sticking straight up like an antenna

lines.narration: You don't say a word. You just nod. Ding. 4,001. Turns out a nod *counts*.
lines.spoken: You don't say a word. You just nod. [deadpan] Ding. Four thousand and one. Turns out a nod counts.
lines.scene: Your head dips once; your number rolls from 4,000 to 4,001 like an old scoreboard; across the office, Pam slow-claps.
lines.camera: Punch close-up on the nod, tilt up to the number, whip to Pam
lines.gag: The ding is as loud as a church bell; coffee cups shake

lines.narration: So you stop nodding too. Now you just stand there, like a lamp with *anxiety*.
lines.scene: One shot: you frozen still at the bus stop, in the lift, at a party, while people wave at you.
lines.camera: Slow lateral glide past you in three places
lines.gag: Someone hangs their coat on you

lines.narration: But it works. She notices you never brag, never fake, and she cancels on the nephew to have dinner with *you*.
lines.scene: Coffee shop: she slides you a cup with 'DINNER?' on the sleeve; in the background Pam reads a text, her jaw drops.
lines.camera: Insert on the cup, rack focus to Pam's face
lines.gag: Pam's face fills red from the chin up into the beehive

lines.narration: Then, at dinner, she asks the question you've been dreading: "Do you like my *band*?"
lines.scene: Candle-lit restaurant at night. Behind her, a poster: four people with kazoos, 'THE KAZOO-NAMI, LIVE'. At the next table, Pam, alone, grinning, staring at your number.
lines.camera: Over her shoulder to you, then push to the poster, then Pam
lines.gag: Pam is at the next table with a napkin tucked in, ready to enjoy the show

lines.narration: Her band is four people with *kazoos*.
lines.scene: Flash insert: the band on a tiny stage, cheeks puffed, one kazoo blowing out a single sad note card.
lines.camera: Hard cut insert, creep-in
lines.gag: A single sad note floats out of a kazoo

lines.narration: One lie, and she'll see it. So for the first time in your life, you tell the truth: "It's *terrible*."
lines.spoken: [tense, hushed] One lie, and she'll see it. So for the first time in your life, you tell the truth: [flatly] "It's terrible."
lines.scene: You, calm and sincere. Total silence. A cricket card in the corner.
lines.camera: Slow push-in on you
lines.gag: A cricket chirps

lines.scene: Your number rolls over, loud as a church bell. Your face drops: white ring eyes.
lines.camera: Whip up to the number, hard cut to your face
lines.gag: Every glass in the restaurant rattles

lines.narration: You see, the number doesn't count what you say. It counts what's true. And deep down, you *love* those kazoos.
lines.scene: Flash insert: you alone in your bedroom at night, secretly playing her band's song on a kazoo, eyes closed, swaying, in a band T-shirt.
lines.camera: Hard cut insert, slow creep-in
lines.gag: You're wearing her band's T-shirt in the flashback

lines.narration: Pam laughs so hard, her beehive falls *off*.
lines.scene: Pam doubled over, slapping the table; the beehive tips and tumbles off her head in slow motion.
lines.camera: Follow the hat down in slow motion
lines.gag: The beehive lands on the lobster in the tank

lines.narration: The 12 was pinned to the beehive. Pam is at *9,000*.
lines.scene: Insert: the fallen beehive, a '12' pinned to its side. Tilt up: above Pam's flat real hair, a giant glowing '9,000' unfolds, so big it bends against the ceiling. The whole restaurant turns to look.
lines.camera: Insert on the hat, then fast tilt up to the 9,000
lines.gag: Pam's 9,000 is so big it scrapes the ceiling
lines.spoken: The twelve was pinned to the beehive. Pam is at nine thousand.

lines.narration: She looks at his number, then at yours, and grins. "You *love* it."
lines.scene: She leans back, triumphant, pulls a kazoo out of her bag and hands it to you; heart cards pop.
lines.camera: Arc around the two of you
lines.gag: She hands you your own kazoo

lines.narration: So, after 3 weeks, you say it out loud: "I *love* it."
lines.spoken: So, after three weeks, you say it out loud: "I love it."
lines.scene: Your MCU across the table; she holds up a kazoo. Your zipper from the cold open is drawn open.
lines.camera: Slow push on you
lines.gag: The zipper on your mouth unzips by itself

lines.narration: No *ding*.
lines.scene: Your 4,002 above your head, perfectly still; the restaurant waits; nothing happens.
lines.camera: Hold on the number, then a tiny push
lines.gag: Every customer is braced, fingers in their ears, for a ding that never comes
